data.title: Health Effects of Long-Term Rapamycin Treatment: The Impact on Mouse Health of Enteric Rapamycin Treatment from Four Months of Age throughout Life
data.authors: Fischer KE; Gelfond JA; Soto VY; Han C; Someya S; Richardson A; Austad SN

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Male and female C57BL/6J mice fed microencapsulated rapamycin (14 ppm) or empty capsules from 4 months of age until death (40 per sex per group); repeated longitudinal health assessments from 16 months
data.finding: Mice of both sexes were fed rapamycin in their food (14 ppm, encapsulated) from 4 months of age until death, 40 per sex per group, and the same animals were tested repeatedly for health measures from 16 months of age. Some measures improved: females had stronger grip at all ages, females kept body mass and fat longer during late-life weight loss, and sleep fragmentation fell in males (with a trend in females). Others did not change, such as stride length and age-related cochlear damage, and male rotarod performance was worse. In body mass, percent fat and resting metabolic rate, rapamycin moved males and females in opposite directions. The study showed that lifelong rapamycin in mice affects healthspan measures in a mixed and strongly sex-specific way rather than improving health across the board. Boundary: C57BL/6J mice only, one dietary dose; survival was reported in a companion paper, not in this one, and mTOR activity was not measured here.
data.abstract_excerpt: Rapamycin, an mTOR inhibitor, has been shown to extend lifespan in a range of model organisms. It has been reported to extend lifespan in multiple strains of mice, administered chronically or acutely early or late in life. The ability of rapamycin to extend health (healthspan) as opposed to life is less well documented. To assess the effects chronic rapamycin treatment on healthspan, enteric rapamycin was given to male and female C57BL/6J mice starting at 4 months of age and continued throughout life.

extracted_findings.intervention: Encapsulated rapamycin in diet, 14 ppm, from 4 months of age for life
extracted_findings.effect: Mixed, sex-specific healthspan effects: better female grip strength and male sleep, worse male rotarod, opposite-sex changes in body mass/fat/metabolic rate
